content.text:
No. The last five commits (all on 2026-09-22) are about printer setup, but two of them go well beyond UX/UI tweaks. They also add new printer-connection behavior and touch OrcaSlicer-owned files. Going back a few more days, the commits cover unrelated areas too.

**Commits since the printer conversation panel was merged (288b9f0dd7, 2026-09-19), newest first:**

| Commit | What it is | Printer setup UX/UI tweak? |
|---|---|---|
| 886098514b Fix Home UI test role query for TypeScript build | One-line test fix | Test fix only |
| 9f739dccf2 Keep printer connection help available and preserve its provider | UI changes, plus new behavior: a runtime override that picks which printer connection provider to use, set through `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent`. It adds 10 lines to the upstream files `GUI_App.cpp`/`.hpp`. It also removes the "Add credentials" commands from `SetupCommands.cpp`. | **Partly.** A real behavior change in an upstream-owned file. |
| 2a07ec0fc7 Give printer setup a focused workspace | Layout, a new design token, and styles | Yes |
| 4d4f9e466b Replace printer summary card with conversational setup guidance | Removes a summary card and changes the model's instructions | Yes (UI plus prompt wording) |
| 67577ad993 Add optional printer connection after saving named printers | A new feature: "connect later" actions on Home, reuse of Bambu and print-host (network printer) connection settings, and saved printers kept when a connection fails. About 230 lines in `OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp` and about 140 in `PrinterConversation.cpp`. | **No.** A feature, not a tweak. |
| b361b84773 Skip automatic setup wizard in JusPrin shell | Stops Orca's first-run setup wizard from opening at startup when the JusPrin shell is active. It adds a flag check to the upstream file `GUI_App.cpp`. | Related (first-run printer setup), but a startup behavior change |
| a7bb15ef9d Configure Codex sandbox mode | One line in `.codex/config.toml` | **No.** Tooling config. |
| ee1bb889a2 Give the Prepare canvas its tools and values back, in a corner row | A new viewport toolbar and value panel (about 2,000 lines), including small additions to the upstream files `GLCanvas3D` and `GizmoObjectManipulation.hpp` | **No.** Unrelated canvas work. |
| a975c79be6 Printer conversation panel: opener wording, photo previews, … Bambu spool simulation | Mostly polish of the printer panel, plus fake Bambu printer spool simulation for testing | Mostly yes, plus test tooling |
| 86d71f3e2c, e00729f58e | An AGENTS.md rule about temporary docs, and removal of a handoff doc | **No.** Repo housekeeping. |

**If you're thinking of reviewing or squashing these as one "printer setup polish" batch:**
- Pull out ee1bb889a2 (canvas toolbar) and a7bb15ef9d (Codex config). Neither is about printer setup.
- Review 67577ad993 and 9f739dccf2 as features, not tweaks. Both change how printers connect, not just how setup looks.
- Three commits touch OrcaSlicer-owned files, which the fork has to re-resolve at every rebase: b361b84773 and 9f739dccf2 (`GUI_App.cpp`/`.hpp`) and ee1bb889a2 (`GLCanvas3D`, `GizmoObjectManipulation.hpp`). Only 9f739dccf2's message includes the rebase evidence that `fork-stewardship.md` asks for.

The working tree also has a large set of uncommitted printer-panel changes (for example, `PrinterConnection.tsx` is deleted and `replyChoices.ts` is new). I didn't include those because they aren't commits yet.

input.description: Show the upstream-file diffs in the three commits

content.text:
All three commits only add lines to upstream OrcaSlicer files. None of them deletes or moves an upstream line. Each addition is a default-off hook that the JusPrin shell turns on, so stock OrcaSlicer behaves the same unless the fork sets it. In total they add about 29 lines across five upstream files.

## b361b84773: Skip automatic setup wizard (4 lines)

This lets the JusPrin shell stop Orca's first-run setup wizard, because the Home screen handles first-run printer setup instead.

`GUI_App.hpp` gets a new public flag that defaults to on:
```cpp
+    // Presentation policy for automatic setup only; explicit run_wizard calls remain available.
+    bool            show_config_wizard_on_startup { true };
```
`GUI_App.cpp`, at the top of `config_wizard_startup()`:
```cpp
+    if (!show_config_wizard_on_startup)
+        return false;
```
The shell turns the flag off when it installs and restores the saved value when it uninstalls. The wizard can still be opened on purpose.

## 9f739dccf2: Printer connection provider override (10 lines)

A "printer agent" is the network backend Orca uses to talk to a printer, such as Bambu or a print host like Moonraker. Stock Orca picks it from the selected printer profile. This hook lets JusPrin pick it explicitly for a printer connection instead.

`GUI_App.hpp` adds `#include <utility>` and a new runtime-only field that is empty by default:
```cpp
+    // An explicit monitor connection may select a provider independently of slicing.
+    // Empty IDs retain the stock profile-driven selection. Runtime only.
+    std::pair<std::string, std::string> printer_agent_override;
```
`GUI_App.cpp`, inside `switch_printer_agent()`, after Orca has chosen an agent from the profile and before it checks that the agent is registered:
```cpp
+    // Resolve an explicit connection through the same switch/refresh/selection path.
+    if (!printer_agent_override.first.empty()) {
+        effective_agent_id = printer_agent_override.first;
+        cloud_agent_id = printer_agent_override.second;
+    }
```
This is the most rebase-sensitive of the three changes. The commit message says newer upstream code makes `effective_agent_id` a `const` and resolves the cloud agent differently. So on the next rebase this hook can't simply be kept as written. It has to be moved to a point before upstream creates the provider.

## ee1bb889a2: Prepare canvas toolbar (15 lines)

These are two hooks so the fork's own canvas toolbar and value panel can draw on the 3D view and reuse Orca's reset logic.

`GLCanvas3D.hpp` adds a drawing callback that is empty by default, plus a setter:
```cpp
+    // JusPrin: extra ImGui content drawn every frame, inside the frame's ImGui
+    // pass and whether or not the legacy overlays are hidden. Empty by default.
+    std::function<void()> m_overlay_renderer;
...
+    void set_overlay_renderer(std::function<void()> renderer) { m_overlay_renderer = std::move(renderer); set_as_dirty(); }
```
`GLCanvas3D.cpp`, in `render()`, right after the normal overlays are drawn:
```cpp
+    if (m_overlay_renderer)
+        m_overlay_renderer();
```
`GizmoObjectManipulation.hpp` adds public wrappers around three existing private reset functions, so the fork calls Orca's code instead of copying it:
```cpp
+    void reset_position() { reset_position_value(); }
+    void reset_rotation(bool to_value_when_tool_opened) { reset_rotation_value(to_value_when_tool_opened); }
+    void reset_scale() { reset_scale_value(); }
```

**Summary:** the setup-wizard hook and the canvas hooks are small, and should be easy to carry through a rebase. The printer connection override is the one likely to need hand-porting, because newer upstream code rewrote the same function. Only 9f739dccf2's commit message includes the rebase-check evidence (a test merge against upstream) that `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md` asks for. The other two commits don't record it.

content.text:
I've read the code that sets and uses each of the three hooks. Here's what they do together.

If the JusPrin shell is not running, the three commits change nothing: every hook defaults to off and stock OrcaSlicer behaves as before. When the shell is running, they change three things: how the app starts, which network backend talks to Bambu printers, and what is drawn on the 3D view. The one real side effect I found is that the Bambu connection choice stays in force for the rest of the session, even after the user switches to a non-Bambu printer.

## Stock OrcaSlicer (shell not installed)

No behavior change.
- The wizard flag defaults to `true`.
- The printer connection override defaults to empty.
- The overlay callback defaults to empty.
- The reset wrappers only forward to the existing private functions.

A shell-harness check (`tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp:1265`) confirms the override stays empty in stock mode. The cost is 29 added lines across 5 upstream files: `GUI_App.cpp/.hpp`, `GLCanvas3D.cpp/.hpp` and `GizmoObjectManipulation.hpp`. No upstream lines were deleted or moved.

## With the JusPrin shell running

1. **The startup wizard is suppressed.** Orca's first-run setup wizard no longer opens automatically, and the Home screen handles first-run printer setup instead. The wizard still opens when asked: JusPrin's own "set it up myself" path calls `run_wizard(RR_USER, SP_PRINTERS)` directly (`OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:197`). The shell restores the flag on uninstall and on window destroy.

2. **Connecting a Bambu printer pins the Bambu backend.** Connecting a Bambu printer from the printer panel (`OrcaPrinterBackend::prepare_connection`) sets the override to the Bambu agent, or to the fake Bambu agent in test mode. It then calls `switch_printer_agent()` and starts device discovery. On uninstall the shell restores the saved override and re-runs `switch_printer_agent()` only if the override changed.

3. **The 3D view gets an extra drawing layer.** The fork's viewport toolbar draws in every frame after Orca's normal overlays, including while Orca's legacy overlays are hidden. The value panel's reset buttons call Orca's own rotation and scale reset code rather than copies of it. The callback is cleared when the canvas presentation detaches (`CanvasPresentationController.cpp:36`).

## Side effects and loose ends

- **The Bambu override outlives the Bambu printer.** Upstream Orca picks the printer backend again every time the printer profile changes (`Tab.cpp:2118`) and after the physical printer dialog saves (`PhysicalPrinterDialog.cpp:900`). While the override is set, both of those keep choosing the Bambu agent. Only the Bambu path sets the override, and nothing clears it except shell teardown. So after a user connects a Bambu printer and then selects a Prusa or Klipper profile, Orca stays on the Bambu agent for the rest of the session. The code comment says this is intended so that editing a profile doesn't drop the connection. I have not checked whether it breaks anything for the non-Bambu printer, such as its device tab or upload. That's worth a quick run with the fake Bambu simulator plus a Klipper profile.
- **`reset_position()` is unused.** It's one of the three new wrappers in `GizmoObjectManipulation.hpp`, and nothing in the fork calls it. Only the rotation and scale wrappers are used (`ToolValuePanel.cpp:311, 345, 425`). It's one upstream line with no caller, so it could be removed.
- **Rebase cost.** Only `switch_printer_agent()` is likely to need hand-porting, because newer upstream rewrote that function (per the commit message of 9f739dccf2). The other hooks are short additions at stable points. Only 9f739dccf2 records a test merge against upstream; b361b84773 and ee1bb889a2 don't.
